To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the distribution of the prepositional phrases is different from the distribution of compounds; 2. there is no correlation between the distribution of the meanings of the prepositions and the meanings of the compounds; 3. there is a correlation between the distribution and the meanings of prepositions and the distribution and the semantics of compounds; 4. the algorithm we have developed for automatic classification of prepositions and compounds outperforms state of the art algorithms.

the syntactic and the semantic properties of the preposition are important factors for the automatic interpretation of nominal phrases, and that the syntactic properties of the prepositional phrase are also relevant.

(1) the semantic interpretation of prepositions in nominal phrases and compounds is not a trivial problem, (2) the problem is not language dependent, and (3) the semantic interpretation problem is not solved by the use of a large training set of nominal phrases and their translations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (i) the syntactic and the semantic properties of prepositional constructions in English and Romance languages; (ii) the automatic interpretation of nominal phrases in terms of prepositional semantics; and (iii) a cross linguistic study on the distribution of the meanings of English nominal phrases in Romance languages.
the problem of automatic interpretation of nominal phrases in natural language processing and the role played by prepositions in this task.
the problem of the semantic interpretation for a given nominal phrase or compound, given the context of a sentence and the syntactic structure of the sentence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the context of semantic interpretation of nominal compounds, the prepositional phrase is a syntactic and semantic unit.
the semantic interpretation of English nominal phrases is not as easy as it seems at first glance, and that it is not possible to predict the semantics based on the syntax alone.
the semantic interpretation of prepositional phrases is not straightforward and that a more fine-grained analysis is needed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the semantic interpretation of prepositional nominal phrases and compounds can be achieved with a high degree of accuracy, even if we do not have a priori knowledge of the semantic properties of the prepositions.
the syntactic and the semantic properties of prepositional constructions in nominal phrases and compounds are highly language dependent.

we have developed a new approach that is capable of learning classification rules from a set of nominal phrases and their translations and that it is able to achieve a high level of accuracy for the semantic interpretation of compounds and nominal phrases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a semantic approach to prepositions can help improve the performance in the task of semantic interpretation of nominal compounds and phrases.
the semantic interpretation of English nominal phrases is a challenging task that requires a careful study of the syntactic and the semantic properties of preposition.
, by combining syntactic and semantic information, we obtain an accuracy that exceeds the accuracy obtained by state of the art methods.
